As a newly-formed tropical disturbance Invest 97W (which replaced 
former Invest 95W) continues to move away from the region to the
northwest, the enhanced monsoon surge that was expected to develop
across the Marianas is not likely to return anytime soon. As such,
intense rainfall and significant gusty winds are no longer expected
at this time, so the Special Weather Statement was allowed to expire.
However, a generally moderate southwesterly monsoon pattern will 
continue to bring patchy showers and some thunderstorms through 
Friday night, followed by a momentary resurgence in convection at a 
leading edge of the monsoon trough and embedded col that may bring 
numerous and potentially heavy showers Saturday and Saturday night. 
Conditions will then improve considerably thereafter, with a dry 
spell to ensue around Labor Day.

Marine...
Combined seas of 7 to 9 feet will persist through Friday, to then 
taper down slowly over the weekend as westerly swells and localized
wind waves diminish further. Hazardous surf and high rip current 
risk is expected along west facing reefs of the Marianas through 
Friday afternoon. As such, a High Surf Advisory and a High Rip
Current Risk Statement remain in effect for west facing reefs of the
Marianas. After, surf is expected to drop below hazardous levels,
along with rip current risk falling to moderate as westerly swells 
diminish. Elsewhere, a moderate risk of rip currents is expected to 
persist along north and south facing reefs of the Marianas tonight.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm Krovanh 22W has moved out of the WFO Guam Area of
Responsibility and will no longer be mentioned in the Area Forecast
Discussion unless it comes back into the WFO Guam AOR, which the
forecast track makes a loop that brings it quite close, so a brief
visit cannot be ruled out at this time.

Invest Area 95W has become one with the general monsoon flow. In its
place, a new circulation, Invest Area 97W, has sprung up. 97W is
currently rated by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center as having a LOW
chance of becoming a tropical cyclone within the next 24 hours. The
possibility is there, but it's not all that high, and it will likely
take more than 24 hours. For more information on Invest Area 97W,
please refer to the Tropical Significant Weather Advisory from the
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
A weak westerly monsoonal flow continues over eastern Micronesia with
an convergence in the flow expected to increase rainfall over Pohnpei
and Kosrae for the next two days. Winds for all islands will stay
light to gentle through the end of this week. Majuro remains on the 
fringe of this flow and is expected to stay fairly dry the rest of 
the week and into Saturday. By Sunday the westerlies look to 
restrengthen and shift north over Majuro, bringing increased 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms and potentially gusty 
winds. The increased monsoonal moisture and elevated winds may also 
reach all the way to Kosrae and Pohnpei but this remains less 
certain. Seas are highest around Pohnpei and Kosrae at 4 to 5 ft and
are expected to gradually decrease going into the weekend. Seas at
Majuro are quite low and won't increase until Sunday at the earliest
as the monsoon flow strengthens.

Western Micronesia...
A tropical high and associated ridge continue to bring a dry spell
across western Micronesia for the rest of the week. At Palau and Yap,
mostly dry conditions expected, with briefly low-end scattered 
showers near midnight tonight at Yap. At Chuuk, patchy showers are 
expected to briefly return Saturday and Saturday night, to then 
slowly taper down thereafter as the previously mentioned tropical 
high settles nearly overhead by early next week.

Combined seas of 3 to 4 feet near Palau, are expected to remain as 
such for much of the forecast period. Combined seas of 4 to 5 feet 
near Yap and Chuuk will slowly taper down a few feet by the weekend 
as westerly swells and local winds diminish.
